claims.claim: ALBERT factorizes embeddings from V×H to V×E + E×H with E smaller than H.
claims.verification_note: 23,040,000 versus 3,938,304 example is an independently derived matrix count using V=30000 H=768 E=128, not full-model parameter count.

claims.claim: ALBERT defaults to sharing all Transformer parameters across encoder layers.
claims.verification_note: Paper also considers partial sharing alternatives.

claims.claim: Cross-layer weight sharing does not remove repeated layer computation.
claims.locator: Overview; repeating layers and computational cost
claims.verification_note: Parameter memory and FLOPs are distinct resources.

claims.claim: Sentence Order Prediction uses consecutive document segments as positive examples and swaps those segments for negatives.
claims.verification_note: Contrasts BERT NSP randomly sourced different-document negative segments.

claims.claim: Original paper Table 1 lists BERT-base 108M, ALBERT-base 12M, BERT-large 334M, ALBERT-large 18M.
claims.verification_note: Numbers match specified configurations, not broad model family or later checkpoint counts.

claims.claim: ALBERT-large training throughput is approximately 1.7 times BERT-large under compared TPU setup.
claims.verification_note: Not generalized to inference throughput or arbitrary hardware.
